input.question: Where was Deodato primarily active in his career?

documents.text: Deodato Orlandi Deodato Orlandi (active 1284-1315, died before 1331) was an Italian painter who was active in Lucca and Pisa. His work marks the transition from the Italo-Byzantine painting of the 13th century to the Giotto-inspired style of the 14th century. Orlandi was active in Lucca and Pisa between 1284 and 1315. He primarily painted religious-themed works on commissions for churches. Some of his works show a Byzantine art style, and an influence of Giotto can also be seen. He painted frescos for the San Piero a Grado church which was commissioned by the Caetani family for the 1300 jubilee.
